'''Roberto Garza''' (born March 26, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] and [[Center (American football)|center]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas A&M–Kingsville Javelinas football|Texas A&M–Kingsville Javelinas]] and was selected by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in the fourth round (99th overall) of the [[2001 NFL draft]], and in 2005, joined the [[Chicago Bears]], spending ten seasons with the team. Despite being an offensive lineman, a position not typically glorified in football, Garza was a fan favorite among [[Hispanic Americans]] across the United States.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/garza-represents-growing-impact-of-nfl-on-hispanic-community-09000d5d80b4d376|title=Garza represents the growing impact of NFL on Hispanic community|website=[[NFL.com]] }}</ref>

'''Rocky Rasley''' (born April 27, 1947) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1969 to 1976.  He attended [[South High School (Bakersfield, California)|Bakersfield's South High School]] and [[Bakersfield College]] before playing [[college football]] for the [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State Beavers]] under [[Dee Andros]] during the "Giant Killers" season of 1967.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://oregonstate.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=121020|title=BeaversEdge – Season of the Giant Killers – Final Thoughts|date=27 August 2002|access-date=July 10, 2007|archive-date=April 1, 2005|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050401013206/http://oregonstate.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=121020|url-status=dead}}</ref>  The entire 1967 squad was later inducted into the Oregon Sports Hall of Fame.<ref name=oshof>{{cite web |url=http://www.oregonsportshall.org/inductee-members.html |publisher=Oregon Sports Hall of Fame |title=Hall of Fame Roll of Honor Members |accessdate=May 5, 2011 |url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727152755/http://www.oregonsportshall.org/inductee-members.html |archivedate=July 27, 2011 }}</ref>  Rasley was also inducted into the Bob Elias Kern County Sports Hall of Fame.<ref name=kcshof>{{cite web |url=http://kcsportshalloffame.org/inductees/rocky-rasley/ |publisher=Kern County Sports Hall of Fame |title=Hall of Fame Inductee Rocky Rasley |accessdate=November 30, 2011}}</ref>

Rasley was one of five Beavers selected in the [[1969 NFL/AFL draft]], and was selected in the ninth round (216th overall) by the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web| url=http://www.osubeavers.com/pdf7/17831.pdf?ATCLID=153842&SPSID=27968&SPID=1952&DB_OEM_ID=4700 | title=Beavers in the pros | access-date=2006-08-14 | archive-date=2016-03-03 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303231658/http://www.osubeavers.com/pdf7/17831.pdf?ATCLID=153842&SPSID=27968&SPID=1952&DB_OEM_ID=4700 | url-status=dead}}</ref>  He played with the Lions for the 1969 and 1970 seasons, was on the Lions' taxi-squad during 1971, and rejoined the team for the 1972 and 1973 seasons.<ref>[http://beckys-place.com/2005images/rasleybio.jpg Rocky Rasley]</ref>  He then went to the [[New Orleans Saints]] for a season, followed by a season with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].  Rasley was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the [[1976 NFL expansion draft]], but did not make the active roster and wound up playing for the [[San Francisco 49ers]] his last season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://beckys-place.com/60rasley.html|title = Seattle Seahawks Spirit of 1976 Page}}</ref>

Prior to joining the NFL, Rasley was a competitive wrestler. He finished 6th in the heavyweight (+100 kg) weight class at the [[1969 FILA Wrestling World Championships]] in [[freestyle wrestling]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iat.uni-leipzig.de/datenbanken/dbfoeldeak/start.php|title=Wrestling Database}}</ref> Rasley also wrestled for the [[Oregon State Beavers wrestling]] team, and was a letterman in 1968.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://osubeavers.nmnathletics.com//pdf6/26123.pdf?SPSID=37974&SPID=1958&DB_OEM_ID=4700 | title=Let us ask you something. And tell us the truth. | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120721222532/http://osubeavers.nmnathletics.com//pdf6/26123.pdf?SPSID=37974&SPID=1958&DB_OEM_ID=4700 | archive-date=2012-07-21 }}</ref>

He was selected by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the first round (25th overall) of the [[1986 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1986 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1986/draft.htm |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> A 1982 graduate of [[South Oak Cliff High School]] and former player for [[Southern Methodist University]],<ref name="dmnsports">[http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/highschools/leaderboard/schoolhome.html?page=alum&sid=292 "My High School: South Oak Cliff,"] ''The Dallas Morning News'' sports section online.</ref> Jones played in 11 seasons for the Bucs and [[Cincinnati Bengals]] from 1986 to 1996.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rod Jones Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JoneRo22.htm |access-date=2024-03-19 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Running for the [[SMU Mustangs track and field]] program, he was an All-American in the 400 meters, and won national titles with the [[4 × 400 meter relay at the NCAA Division I Outdoor Track and Field Championships|1,600-meter relay]] team in 1984 and 1986. The latter occurred only four days before his report to Buccaneers training camp. He won SMU's Big Hit award in his last two football seasons, where he was nicknamed "K.O." for his hard-hitting play.<ref>Kaufman, Michelle. "His primary goal is secondary". St. Petersburg Times. June 12, 1986</ref> He was later named as one of the players who had received slush-fund money in the scandal that resulted in SMU receiving the [[Southern Methodist University football scandal|"death penalty"]] from the [[NCAA]].<ref>Sullivan, Robert and Craig Neff. "Shame on You, SMU". Sports Illustrated. March 9, 1987</ref>

Jones was the first of the 1986 first-round draft picks to sign with his team. There was concern that his contract, described as "terrible" by sports agents, would set a bad precedent in negotiations that year. It featured a high signing bonus and a salary far below the previous year's average.<ref>Steele, David. "Rod Jones' salary 'terrible'". St. Petersburg Evening Independent. July 16, 1986</ref> He was inserted immediately into the Bucs' starting lineup as a rookie. In his professional career, he appeared in 146 games, intercepting 10 passes for 49 yards.

Jones' claim to fame is having caught [[Bo Jackson]], who appeared to have a touchdown, from behind after an 88-yard run in 1990.<ref>{{cite web | last=Kantowski | first=Ron | title=5 things about Bo Jackson getting caught from behind | website=Las Vegas Review-Journal | date=2020-05-09 | url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/raiders/5-things-about-bo-jackson-getting-caught-from-behind-2024743/ | access-date=2025-06-29}}</ref>

'''Victor Kenneth "Rocky" Klever''' (born July 10, 1959) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] for the [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Raised in [[Anchorage, Alaska]], he played [[college football]] for the [[Montana Grizzlies football|Montana Grizzlies]] and was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the ninth round of the [[1982 NFL draft]]. Klever played his entire career with the Jets, over which he served as a backup in a variety of roles and started as a [[tight end]] over several seasons.

Klever played as a [[quarterback]] at [[West Anchorage High School]], where he won the state title in 1975 and was named to the all-state team (an honorific team composed of the best players in the state) in 1976 and 1977. Attending the University of Montana, he converted to a [[Halfback (American football)|tailback]] and set a school record for most career rushing yards which stood for approximately twenty years. 

The Jets originally intended Kelver to play as a [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]], though he converted to [[tight end]] in 1984. After suffering two [[disc herniation|herniated discs]] and missing the entire 1988 season, Klever was [[waivers (American football)|waived]] (an NFL process in which a team releases a player and makes him available to all other NFL teams) prior to the next season.

He was inducted into the [[hall of fame]] of the University of Montana in 2016, the Montana Football Hall of Fame in 2018, and the Alaska High School Hall of Fame in 2006. {{asof|2020}}, Klever lives in [[Linwood, New Jersey]].

'''Rocco Ray Moore''' (March 31, 1955 - December 21, 2007)<ref name="obit">{{cite web|title=Former Bronco Great Rocco Moore Passes Away|url=http://www.wmubroncos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4600&ATCLID=1356319|website=wmubroncos.com|publisher=[[Western Michigan University]]|accessdate=21 July 2016|date=27 December 2007|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304193149/http://www.wmubroncos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4600&ATCLID=1356319|archivedate=4 March 2016}}</ref> was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).
